title: Dissecting Structural and Lexical Shortcut Learning in Phishing Detection: Evidence-to-Claim Audit

claims.section: Section III: Model Architectures and Baseline Evaluation
claims.statement: FusionNN achieves a 5-fold cross-validation macro F1-score of 0.9952 (ROC-AUC 0.9996, ECE 0.0042) on the baseline dataset.

claims.section: Section III: Model Architectures and Baseline Evaluation
claims.statement: XGBoost achieves a 5-fold cross-validation macro F1-score of 0.9940 (ROC-AUC 0.9992, ECE 0.0061).

claims.section: Section III: Model Architectures and Baseline Evaluation
claims.statement: DistilBERT achieves a 5-fold cross-validation macro F1-score of 0.9915 (ROC-AUC 0.9984, ECE 0.0089).
Under structural artifact stripping, FusionNN performance drops from 0.9952 to 0.3594 macro F1-score (delta = -0.6358), while ECE degrades to 0.5843.
DistilBERT exhibits superior resilience under artifact stripping, retaining a macro F1-score of 0.7931 (delta = -0.1984).

claims.section: Section V: External Transfer and Out-of-Distribution Generalization
claims.statement: On out-of-distribution external dataset transfer (N=2,500), FusionNN macro F1 drops to 0.4908 while DistilBERT retains 0.8124 (Wilcoxon p < 0.001).

claims.section: Section VI: Adversarial Obfuscation Stress Testing
claims.statement: Under multi-tactic adversarial attack, FusionNN F1 deteriorates to 0.1224, whereas DistilBERT preserves 0.6412 F1-score.
